purpose: Prevent duplicate/stale substantive authority without rejecting harmless scheduler jitter that can increase utilization.
rule: Treat schedule timestamps as target wake times, not exact-dispatch correctness goals. An early invocation is not automatically fenced. If no conflicting live authority/lease exists and durable state can be claimed monotonically, accept the wake and continue useful work immediately. Fence only when accepting it would create duplicate substantive authority, stale-state rollback, or destructive overlap. Never classify harmless early/late jitter itself as a failure.

timing_semantics.normal_provisional: eligible wake reference + exactly 11 minutes (660 seconds)
timing_semantics.premature_tolerance_human: No fixed early-jitter rejection threshold; safety/authority conflict determines fencing.

evidence_basis: Epoch 85 invocation was observed at 08:28:42 KST while the predecessor's live-verified fast due remained 08:29:51 KST, 1 minute 9 seconds (69 seconds) later. Blind provisional rearm would have canceled the still-pending P0-B test, so the pending due was restored before it elapsed.
rollback: Restore strict pre-due fencing only if measured overlap/duplicate side effects exceed the utilization benefit.
